chiefs_of_defence_staff.name: Jonathan Vance
chiefs_of_defence_staff.notable: Six-year CDS. Presided over Operation Honour response to sexual misconduct in the CAF. Was himself charged in 2021 with obstruction of justice relating to a former relationship; pleaded guilty 2022, received conditional discharge. His tenure is the central locus of the 2015-2022 military accountability crisis.

chiefs_of_defence_staff.name: Wayne Eyre
chiefs_of_defence_staff.notable: Initially acting CDS during the Vance-McDonald crisis (Art McDonald was stood aside pending investigation before returning to the role). Confirmed as CDS November 2021. Responsible for the initial CAF response to the Arbour Report.

chiefs_of_defence_staff.name: Jennie Carignan
chiefs_of_defence_staff.notable: First female CDS in Canadian history. Previously led Chief of Professional Conduct and Culture (CPCC) on sexual-misconduct reform. Appointed after Sajjan-era cultural reforms were judged insufficient.

judge_advocates_general.name: Blaise Cathcart
judge_advocates_general.notable: JAG covering the pre-Deschamps period through the 2015 Deschamps Report. Senior military legal adviser to the government for 7 years.

judge_advocates_general.name: Genevieve Bernatchez
judge_advocates_general.notable: First female JAG. Five-year tenure spanning Operation Honour, Vance's charges, and the Arbour Report. Responsible for legal policy across all CAF discipline matters.

judge_advocates_general.name: Rob Holman
judge_advocates_general.notable: Current JAG. Tenure covers the post-Arbour reforms and the transfer of certain sexual-assault cases from military to civilian jurisdiction.

canadian_forces_provost_marshals.name: Rob Delaney
canadian_forces_provost_marshals.role: Canadian Forces Provost Marshal (Military Police Commander)
canadian_forces_provost_marshals.notable: CFPM during the Deschamps Report period. Head of the Canadian Forces Military Police Group including CFNIS.

canadian_forces_provost_marshals.name: Simon Trudeau
canadian_forces_provost_marshals.notable: CFPM during the Operation Honour implementation and the early period of CFNIS case-volume increases.

canadian_forces_provost_marshals.name: Jeffrey Peck
canadian_forces_provost_marshals.notable: CFPM during the Vance investigation period. Oversaw the CFNIS response to multiple high-profile sexual-misconduct cases.

canadian_forces_provost_marshals.name: Alexander Orr
canadian_forces_provost_marshals.notable: CFPM during the post-Arbour transfer of some sexual-assault cases to civilian jurisdiction. Responsible for CFNIS current operations.

defence_ministers.name: Harjit Sajjan
defence_ministers.notable: Six-year Defence Minister. Cross-axis: also in arms pipeline dossier. Was publicly criticised for handling of the Vance misconduct allegations (reportedly received information in 2018 but did not act until 2021).

defence_ministers.name: Anita Anand
defence_ministers.notable: Defence Minister during the Arbour Report release and subsequent implementation. Commissioned the Arbour review. Later moved to Treasury Board and then Foreign Affairs.

defence_ministers.name: Bill Blair
defence_ministers.notable: Defence Minister during the second year of Arbour implementation. Cross-axis: also in corrections dossier (Public Safety 2019-2021) and arms pipeline dossier.

independent_review_bodies.name: Justice Louise Arbour
independent_review_bodies.notable: Retired Supreme Court justice appointed to conduct the IECR on sexual misconduct in the CAF. Final report May 2022 with 48 recommendations including transferring certain cases to civilian jurisdiction.

independent_review_bodies.name: Marie Deschamps
independent_review_bodies.notable: Retired Supreme Court justice whose 2015 report first documented the scale of sexual misconduct in the CAF. The Deschamps Report triggered Operation Honour.

independent_review_bodies.name: Morris Rosenberg
independent_review_bodies.notable: Former Deputy Minister of Justice. Authored the 2023 report on the implementation of sexual misconduct reforms in the CAF.

timeline.event: Deschamps Report released — first public documentation of sexual misconduct as a systemic issue in the CAF.
Operation Honour launched — CAF's initial response to Deschamps.
Jonathan Vance sworn in as CDS.
Geneviève Bernatchez sworn in as first female JAG.
Minister Sajjan reportedly informed of Vance misconduct allegations but did not act publicly until 2021.
Global News reports sexual-misconduct allegations against CDS Jonathan Vance.
Justice Louise Arbour appointed to lead the Independent External Comprehensive Review.
Jonathan Vance charged with obstruction of justice by the Ontario Provincial Police.
Jonathan Vance pleads guilty to obstruction of justice; conditional discharge.
Arbour Report tabled: 48 recommendations, including transferring some sexual-assault cases to civilian jurisdiction.
Rosenberg implementation report released, flagging uneven implementation of Arbour recommendations.
General Jennie Carignan appointed as first female CDS in Canadian history.

statutory_framework: National Defence Act — R.S.C. 1985, c. N-5
Code of Service Discipline — NDA Part III
oversight_bodies: Military Police Complaints Commission (MPCC) — independent review of MP conduct
Office of the Judge Advocate General — legal oversight
Office of the Chief Military Judge — judicial oversight
Office of the Auditor General — periodic audits of CAF discipline
legislative_response: Bill C-77 (2019) — Declaration of Victims Rights in CAF discipline process
Arbour recommendations implementation ongoing — uneven per Rosenberg
accountability_chain.result_2025: Post-Arbour reforms partially implemented; sexual-assault case transfers to civilian jurisdiction inconsistent; PPCLI and other regiment-level lawsuits continuing; CFNIS handling of retaliation and whistleblower cases still documented in open evidence
